$comment: Inputs for the format-string differential oracle (docs/differential-oracle.md, and the attention belt's D- entry for sub-belt A3). Committed rather than generated so both halves build the identical vector, and small enough to read. Regenerate the vector with scripts/oracle/dump_pyformat.py -- never by hand.
$comment_templates: Grouped by what each group is asking. The groups are: literals and brace escapes; the six names the design's section 6 allowlist permits; names outside it, including the attribute and index reaches the allowlist exists to forbid; positional and auto-numbered fields, which format_map has no arguments for; the three conversions; the format specs a str accepts; the ones it refuses; nested specs, which are expanded one level; and templates that do not parse at all. Every group carries at least one input that RENDERS and one that RAISES, so a half-implemented answer cannot pass by refusing everything or by rendering everything.
$comment_width: No width beyond a few hundred. CPython honours an arbitrary width literally, so a template of {pr:2147483647} makes both halves allocate two gigabytes; the oracle would then measure the allocator rather than the mini-language.
